C-05.1.answer: Every new user-facing doc (README.zh-CN, the tutorials, the FAQ, the comparison page) is added to the lists the claims tests scan, so a refusal code, file name or security word they cite that the code lacks turns those tests red; the tutorial commands were run on a fake home and copied from the real output.
C-05.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every code the user-facing docs name exists in the code

C-05.2.answer: Each command a reader is told to run is a real sakk subcommand: the README command check is extended to the Chinese README and the tutorials, and every exit code or figure quoted was taken from a run on a fake home, not written from memory.
C-05.2.guard: test/release.test.mjs::every command the README shows is a real sakk subcommand

C-06.1.answer: The docs keep the product's own source labels: spend is from local logs, a stop is self-declared, a halt name is typed not signed; the security-word scan covers the new docs so none of them upgrades a self-declared record into a signature.
C-06.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::no user-facing text calls a record signed, immutable or tamper-proof without a mechanism

C-03.1.answer: The extended scans are checked red first: a planted unknown code, a missing file name and the word signed in a copy of a new doc each make the matching claims test fail, and removing the plant makes it pass again.
C-03.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::each backticked file name in the docs appears in the code or the repository

C-03.2.answer: The control is the existing assertion that every scanned file exists and has text; the new docs are added to that same list, so a doc that went missing or empty fails rather than leaving the scan reading nothing.
C-03.2.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every scanned file exists and has text

C-03.3.answer: The checks read the doc text itself and resolve each cited code against the source tree and each command against the CLI's real subcommand list, so a doc cannot pass on paperwork while naming something that does not exist.
C-03.3.guard: test/release.test.mjs::every command the README shows is a real sakk subcommand

C-01.1.answer: A doc listed for scanning that is absent fails the scan instead of being skipped, because the scanned-file assertion reads every listed path and requires text; nothing in this branch treats a missing doc as a pass.
C-01.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every scanned file exists and has text

C-01.2.answer: Deleting a new doc from the tree turns the scanned-file test red because it stays in the scan list; deleting it from the list instead is a visible diff to the test file that review reads, not a silent pass.
C-01.2.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every scanned file exists and has text

C-10.1.answer: Doc accuracy is not left to rule text: the claims and release tests run in npm test, the commit gate and CI, and they read the new docs, so a wrong code, file name or command blocks the merge.
C-10.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every code the user-facing docs name exists in the code

C-10.2.answer: Another route is a doc added later outside the lists; the file-name scan reads every top-level docs markdown by directory listing, and the tutorial folder is added the same way, so a new file there is scanned without anyone editing a list.
C-10.2.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::each backticked file name in the docs appears in the code or the repository

C-02.1.answer: The README's codes, commands and file names are not hand-checked lists: the claims and release tests enumerate every backticked code, file name and sakk command from the doc text and resolve each against the source tree and the CLI's own subcommand table.
C-02.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every code the user-facing docs name exists in the code

C-04.1.guard: none: a docs-only change adds no code path that reads hostile input, so there is no new work to bound
